chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Earl Hines goes off to lead his own band
summary: Earl Hines left Louis to lead his own band at the Grand Terrace, and Gene Anderson took the piano in Dickerson's band at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well how about, how about when now what about, well of course Father Hines got his band in the Grand Terrace? That would be about '28. So he
Yes, but I mean, but why did he not stay with Louis? Was that because ............
He had a chance to go on his own, have his own band.
On his own. And they organised a little small band, well Father Hines got in. See, that's when they had Sid (Catlett), I mean (Cozy) and that bunch. Jack Teagarden.
Earl got pretty, well/in there when you want the Savoy; Earl didn't play with you all.
See Earl was away from the band when they went in the Savoy with (Carroll) Dickerson. Earl was owning his own band. He had gotten him a job. But they got Gene Anderson.
